title: SafeFlowMatcher: Safe and Fast Planning using Flow Matching with Control Barrier Functions
one_liner: A planner that couples fast path generation with mathematical guarantees that the path never violates physical constraints.
lead: Planning algorithms need to be both fast and safe. Flow matching makes planning fast by generating paths in just one or two steps, but it offers no guarantee the paths will avoid obstacles or respect physical limits. SafeFlowMatcher adds a safety layer—a mathematical gate that catches unsafe paths and minimally fixes them while preserving speed.

paras: A robot planning a path from start to goal faces a tradeoff. Old planners guarantee safety by checking every possible position as they build the path—they are slow. Flow matching speeds this up dramatically: it trains a neural model to generate a complete path in one or two steps, skipping the expensive checking. But this speed comes at a cost: the model has never learned what safe actually means, so it cheerfully generates paths that crash into walls or violate force limits.

A beginner might try: train the flow-matching model on only safe paths, so it learns to prefer safety. This sounds reasonable but fails because (1) the model is trained on the latent space (an abstract intermediate representation), not the real world—paths safe in that abstract space are often unsafe when you execute them, and (2) even if the model sees safety during training, the random sampling in flow matching can still produce garbage near constraints, where the learned patterns are weakest.

callout.html: SafeFlowMatcher fixes unsafe paths after the model generates them, using a mathematical gate that enforces constraints with minimal changes to the generated path.

steps.b: Prediction: Flow matching generates a candidate path
steps.text: Run the learned flow model forward in one or two ODE steps to get a draft path from start to goal.
Check which parts of the draft path violate constraints (collision, bounds, force limits).
Formulate a quadratic program: adjust the path's motion only where needed to restore safety.
The quadratic program finds the minimal perturbation to the path vector field that guarantees forward invariance—the path stays safe from this point onward.
Integrate the corrected vector field to get the final path. By construction, it is safe and converges to the goal in finite time.

paras: SafeFlowMatcher changes the path generation process itself. Instead of trusting the flow-matching model's output directly, it adds a second stage—a mathematical correction layer—that refines the path to satisfy constraints.

hidden.h2: Forward invariance: the guarantee that safety holds
hidden.name: forward invariance certificate
paras: Forward invariance is a mathematical property: if the current state is safe, the next state will also be safe. It is not a measurement from data; it is a proof. The paper proves that after applying the correction phase, the resulting path has this property—once safe, always safe.

The paper establishes forward invariance by constructing a barrier certificate: a mathematical function that stays positive along the path whenever the path is in the safe region. If this function is positive, the path cannot escape the safe zone. The correction-phase quadratic program is designed to make this function positive on the executed path, so the safety guarantee holds by construction.

heat.caption: Darker means higher forward-invariance guarantee. Highlights show where the barrier certificate is proven to hold.

reads.html: Forward invariance is a promise: if you are safe now, the next step keeps you safe. It is like a fence that the path can never cross.
The paper constructs a barrier certificate—a Lyapunov-like function—and proves finite-time convergence to the safe set under the corrected flow dynamics.

mechanism.h2: Why two-phase correction achieves safety and speed together
paras: The core insight is that the flow-matching model is good at fast generation but was never trained to enforce hard constraints. Instead of retraining it (slow), SafeFlowMatcher accepts whatever path the model produces and applies a specialized mathematical tool—a quadratic program with barrier functions—that enforces constraints afterward.

This works because the quadratic program is lightweight: it only adjusts the vector field (the direction and speed of motion) in the minimal way needed to keep the path safe. It does not regenerate the entire path; it just refines the model's trajectory. Since the correction is applied only to the executed path—not every latent intermediate—it avoids a problem called distributional drift (when the refined path looks so different from the training distribution that the model breaks). The result is a path that is fast, mathematically proven safe, and smoother than either flow matching or diffusion planning alone.

stages.s: Start and goal positions, constraint list
Flow matching generates candidate path in one step
Quadratic program corrects path minimally to satisfy constraints
Barrier certificate proves the corrected path stays safe
Final path: fast, smooth, and formally safe

math.words: The correction phase solves: minimize the change to the vector field, subject to the barrier certificate staying positive along the path.
math.equation: min ||u - u_FM||^2 subject to h(x(t)) >= 0 for all t in [0, T]
symbols: the corrected vector field (which way to move)
the barrier certificate at position x and time t
the safe region constraint (barrier stays positive)
squared difference (how much change from original)

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose the flow-matching model predicts: move 5 units forward, 2 units left.
This violates a collision constraint at position (5, 2).
The quadratic program computes: move 4.8 units forward, 1.9 units left instead.
The barrier function h(4.8, 1.9) is now positive (safe), with minimal motion adjustment.

math.note: The quadratic program finds the smallest nudge to the path that keeps the barrier certificate positive everywhere.

bars.h2: How different methods trade off speed, safety, and smoothness

charts.title: Diffusion planning (baseline)
charts.note: Slow but careful. Many paths fail because diffusion sampling is noisy near constraints.

charts.title: Flow matching alone
charts.note: Fast and smooth, but lacks safety guarantees. Crashes frequently.

charts.title: SafeFlowMatcher
charts.note: Fast (one extra correction step is negligible), provably safe, and smooth.

items.b: Correction becomes expensive if constraints are very tight.
items.html: If the safe region is tiny or the constraint surface is complex, the quadratic program may require many iterations. In these cases, the speed advantage over diffusion-based planning shrinks.

The barrier function h must be designed for each type of constraint (collision, force, velocity). A poorly designed barrier may claim safety when it does not. This is not a flaw in the paper's theory—the theory assumes a correct barrier—but it places burden on the user to validate h for their domain.

items.b: Flow-matching model must already be roughly good.
items.html: If the flow model generates paths pointing in completely wrong directions, the correction phase must work harder. The method does not rescue a trained-poorly flow model; it assumes the model is already learning the task structure well.

items.b: Done right: barrier functions validated independently.
items.html: When the barrier certificate h is carefully designed and verified for the problem domain, SafeFlowMatcher delivers both speed and formal safety without retraining.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a simple 2D maze planner. Start with a flow-matching model trained to navigate the maze, then run it three ways: (1) pure flow matching, generating paths directly; (2) SafeFlowMatcher with a designed barrier function for collision avoidance. For each, measure: how long the planning takes, how often the path reaches the goal, whether the path violates any walls (using the barrier function h as a ground-truth check).
demo.closing: The demo must show that SafeFlowMatcher's success rate matches the diffusion baseline because the barrier certificate enforces constraints just as strictly, while planning time stays fast because the correction is applied only once per path, not inside the iterative diffusion loop.
